input.description: Reproduce a pull failing midway with fake IndexedDB and GitHub

content.text:
I found the bug and reproduced it. A pull that fails partway leaves that device saying "in sync" while it's missing the newest files, and it stays that way until someone commits again.

## Main cause: a pull that fails partway

`pullNow()` in `shared/github.js:124` saves the commit's ETag (a version marker GitHub returns) as soon as the first check succeeds. Only after that does it download the file list and the changed files. If the connection drops at that point (your `NetworkError`), the device has already marked that commit as pulled. Every later pull then gets `304 Not Modified` and reports **"in sync"**. The files from that commit never arrive.

It only clears when anyone commits something new, so the newest tickets are the ones that stay missing. That matches what you're seeing.

I reproduced it in node with a fake IndexedDB and a fake GitHub (`/tmp/claude-1000/-home-max-ws-mine/d6feedc0-ad9b-411b-806d-156b95955d28/scratchpad/repro.mjs`):
```
pull 1: NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.
pull 2: {"changed":0,"unchanged":true}      ← "in sync"
mirror: [ 'notes/old.md' ]                  ← notes/new.md never arrives
```
The push path has the same problem, because a push that collides with a newer commit pulls before retrying (`github.js:258`).

**About the `NetworkError` itself:** I checked whether last commit's `cache: 'no-store'` breaks GitHub's CORS check in Firefox. It doesn't: headless Firefox got HTTP 200 in all four cache modes. So it's an ordinary dropped request, likely a phone PWA pulling on focus before its network is back. That's harmless by itself. The real problem is that the next pull doesn't recover from it.

## Likely contributors to tickets vanishing (from reading the code, not reproduced)

1. **The file list comes from the branch name, not the commit just checked** (`github.js:128`). If the branch moves between the two requests, the saved ETag and the file list can belong to different commits.
2. **Two apps open at once on one device.** Calendar and notes share one local database, but each only queues sync work against itself. Say notes pushes a new note while calendar is mid-pull with an older file list. Calendar then deletes the new note from local storage, because it's not in that list and no longer waiting to be pushed. It may also save the older ETag, and combined with the main bug the note stays gone from local storage.

## Proposed fix (small, in `pullNow`)
- Save the ETag **last**, after all downloads and deletions have succeeded.
- Fetch the file list by the exact commit the check returned, not by branch name. That fixes point 1 as well.

Point 2 needs a lock shared across tabs, such as `navigator.locks.request('mine-sync', …)` around the sync step in `shared/sync.js`. That's about 3 lines.

**Already-stuck devices:** they'll catch up on the next commit from anywhere. Saving any small edit from that device also works.

Should I apply the first fix (and the lock too?), with a regression test and the doc update in `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md`?
yes, apply both fixes with the lock

input.description: Read the pull and sync sections of the technical doc

result.output:
[REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md#markdown-bodies).

## Fetching the repo

There is one read path, `pull`, and it is also the first mirror: with no stored ETag it fetches
the tree and every blob in it. A GraphQL query returning a folder's contents and blob SHAs in a
single request was built and measured — cost 1, 145 files in 6 s — and then never wired in,
because `pull` already handled the first run and the empty repo. It was deleted rather than left
as a second way to do the same thing; against a mirror measured in single-digit MB, fetched once
per device, the request count it saved was not worth a path nothing exercised.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota, and no ETag at all means a first mirror.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths — except
   a path still in the queue, which is a save made while the pull ran and not in the remote yet.

**Every request is `cache: 'no-store'`.** GitHub answers `cache-control: max-age=60`, and a push
clears the stored ETag, so the pull after it is a plain GET the browser would answer from its own
cache: the commit and the tree from before the push. That pull then deletes the note just pushed
from the mirror, and it reappears a minute later. A conditional GET is unaffected — a request
carrying its own `If-None-Match` bypasses the cache anyway, so the 304 still reaches the code.

**Always the whole repo, and deliberately no way to ask for one app's folder.** There is a single
`commitEtag` for the whole mirror, so a pull restricted to `diary/` would store the ETag of a
commit it had not mirrored, and the calendar's next pull would 304 against it and never see its
own files again. `pull()` used to take a prefix that did exactly this; no caller passed one, and
it was the parameter a second app would have reached for first. A per-folder pull would need a
per-folder ETag, and what it saves is one conditional GET.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

**A queue is drained first and the pull waits for it**, and the pull runs only if the drain got
through: whatever fails a drain — the token, the network — fails a pull too, and pulling over a
dirty queue rewrites the mirror underneath the changes still in it.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

retry, so one such item wedges the queue for good. A file moved or deleted before the queue ever
drained is exactly that case, because a move is a delete of a path GitHub never saw: with the
date in the path, changing an unpushed entry's date queues `del <old>` for a path that was only
ever local. Dropping it is also what was asked for — the file is gone locally and GitHub has
nothing to remove. If every queued item turns out to be such a no-op, the queue is cleared and
no commit is made.

This is also why a concurrent delete from another device heals itself: the listing is re-read on
every attempt, so the path is gone from it and the entry is dropped rather than refused.

**A matching text is a receipt, not a conflict.** A drain that died between the ref update and
the queue being cleared leaves items behind whose base SHA no longer matches — because the remote
now holds our own commit. Those are dropped, not forked: the blob is fetched in that branch
anyway, so comparing it costs no request, and without the comparison the app forks its own
committed work into `.conflict` files on the next attempt.

**Every attempt is retried.** The queue is never a reason to skip a drain, including on 401/403:
the error is reported and recorded, and the next open or focus tries again. The user needs one
thing from a failure, which is to be told what it was.

content.text:
I've applied both fixes and the cross-tab lock, and the full test suite passes. Nothing is committed yet.

**Changes:**
- **Pull saves its version marker last** (`shared/github.js`). The commit's ETag is now stored only after every file has downloaded. A pull that drops partway leaves the old marker, so the next pull fetches that commit again and the missing tickets arrive.
- **File list comes from the commit just checked** (`shared/github.js`). It's now fetched by that commit's tree SHA instead of the branch name, so the list and the saved ETag can't belong to different commits.
- **One sync at a time across all tabs and installed apps** (`shared/sync.js`). Each sync attempt now holds a browser lock named `mine-sync`. Calendar and notes open side by side can no longer push and pull at the same time over the shared local data. The lock needs a reasonably recent browser (Firefox 96+, Safari 15.4+, current Chrome).
- **Service worker version** bumped to `2026-11-26.14`, so installed PWAs pick up the new code.
- **Docs:** `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` describes the new pull order and the lock. `TEST-REQUIREMENTS.md` describes the new check.

**Regression check:** I added section 8 to `test/check-mine.mjs`. It fakes GitHub inside the page, makes the first file-list request fail with the same `NetworkError` you saw, and has two sync lines refresh at once. Its six assertions all pass with the fixes. I temporarily reverted `shared/github.js` and `shared/sync.js`, and all six failed, including "got 2, want 1" for requests in flight at the same time.

A device that's already stuck heals once it runs the new version: the next commit from anywhere, or any save from that device, makes it pull again.
